# Routing Reference Attribution

Vary AI adapts selected routing, catalog, gateway, and interface behavior from
[yetone/magpie](https://github.com/yetone/magpie), Copyright (c) 2026 yetone,
under the MIT License. The complete copyright and permission notice is retained
unchanged in [LICENSE](LICENSE). Renamed local assets and modules retain this
attribution.

## Pinned source revisions

- `c5b9e448a8bc9bc2a1bf6704e5d8bb3384d084a6`: quick-panel allowance cards,
  reviewed in `internal/gui/assets/app.js` (`renderPanelQuota`,
  `panelQuotaCard`), `app.css` and the panel quota lazy-loading/refresh tests.
  Vary adapts the provider headings, account cards, window rings, used/remaining
  toggle, named reset times and per-card refresh into its existing React query
  and quota readers. It does not copy quota history, remote sharing, arrangement
  controls or account credit/reset policies.
  The same revision's `internal/provider/balance_probe.go`, `balance.go` and
  `balance_probe_test.go` inform relay probe ordering, six-hour missing-interface
  caching and omission of unsupported cards. Vary reuses its bounded Rust
  read-only probe and React query cache, preserving reported zero balances,
  retryable failures and stale readings instead of presenting unsupported relays
  as subscription errors.

existing token; a new connection writes its new token. No fixed Magpie token or
cross-agent credential acceptance is adopted.

## Compatibility literals

Daily reward protocol behavior was reviewed in `magpie-community/plugins`
`packages/qoder/index.mjs` (Git blob `5785a7c0c8f68493d16d315c1063d1514da09a76`),
`packages/trae/index.mjs` (blob `15d2389db8ebb07fcb30b46fd5f0c65f4a11da5f`),
and `packages/zcode/index.mjs` (blob `13cbbe330f3896621e492b4f69f621ed16664f84`).
VaryAI independently implements campaign-window accounting, official daily-credit
IPC and explicit gift-plan actions. Native interfaces were additionally checked
against the installed Qoder CN 0.4.8/0.5.3, TRAE CN 3.4.14/3.4.15 and ZCode 3.16.3 clients and
ZCode's public `docs/marketing-touch-client.md` contract. No plugin implementation
is copied. Qoder account reuse additionally follows the installed client's
`product.json`, encrypted auth schema and Electron/Chromium's macOS `v10` format.
OS-approved native account access is preferred, with an optional independent
browser grant. Native refresh tokens are not rotated, and CAPTCHA remains in the
official client.

Additional subscription integrations reference `internal/provider/google.go`,
`chatgpt_api.go`, `claude_signin.go`, `claude_dirs.go`, `claude_code_models.go`,
and `internal/gateway/claude_subscription.go` / `codeassist.go` at revision
`1d0fc2bb08c51d8711759694189b8a1d92ee3a1e`. The Gemini CLI and Antigravity
SVGs come from that revision's `internal/gui/assets/icons` (Lobe Icons,
MIT licensed). Vary's Rust implementation uses its own account storage and
shared protocol bridge; it does not implement Magpie's persistent Claude runs.

Routing candidate names additionally follow `internal/provider/keys.go`
(`RestKeys` and `severalOn`), `internal/gateway/trace.go` (`weighed`), and the
routing plugin's `who` / `makeRow` at Magpie revision
`1d0fc2bb08c51d8711759694189b8a1d92ee3a1e`: one enabled key uses the supplier
name, while a shared pool uses key names with masked-key fallbacks.

Internal selectors, variable names, assets, and design filenames use Vary or
descriptive names. A few external format identifiers remain literal so existing
files and integrations continue to work:

- Provider imports retain the source ID `magpie`, the optional IPC argument
  `magpiePath`, the default `~/.config/magpie` / `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/magpie`
  locations, and recognition of `magpie-models.json` and the `magpie` provider
  identity when avoiding imports of a client's own generated gateway entries.
- Portable routing-group JSON retains `magpie: "routing-group"`, version 1,
  and accepts the `magpie/` model-reference prefix.
- Compatibility tests retain those exact synthetic identifiers. They must not
  be replaced with escaped or dynamically assembled spellings to conceal them.

The renderer labels the portable source **Magpie** and places it first. Import reads
the original source files, keeps credentials in the backend, and does not modify
the source application.

- `c3593dc4944b91819ed12c601b0f2e844b804b5e`: desktop discovery behavior
  reviewed in `internal/agent/desktopapp.go`, `workbuddy.go` and
  `workbuddy_app_test.go`: application identities, both WorkBuddy builds,
  application subfolders and Spotlight fallback. Vary uses its own Rust
  discovery and React window-activation refresh implementation.

## Codex service-tier publication

At `465928bccea4fec3537edd6280f7cabb9a0c5bad`, the `ownTiers`, `namedTiers`, and
entry-tier publication behavior in `internal/codexcat/codexcat.go`, together with
`internal/agent/codex_catalog_tiers_test.go`, inform VaryAI's independent Rust
service-tier adapter. VaryAI normalizes supported public fields, keeps local and
served catalogs consistent, and uses common tiers for routing groups rather than
Magpie's any-fast-member rule because group routing is not tier-aware. No upstream
source implementation is copied.

At the same revision, `internal/provider/modelprefs.go` (`Label`, `Labels`) and
`internal/provider/codex_models.go` (`codexApart`) inform the separation of short
picker labels from stable source/model identity and visible-list disambiguation.
VaryAI independently abbreviates automatically named personal-account sources,
keeps explicit custom names, and numbers colliding visible sources without adding
account email addresses to model labels.

## Subscription protocol repairs

The managed Grok subscription transport independently follows
[magpie-community/plugins](https://github.com/magpie-community/plugins),
`packages/grok/index.mjs` at
`41e90a18d3affc7487460d032b0cdc5e09b20ebb`: CLI proxy endpoints, client headers,
model/context-window identities, credit billing and rejected-token renewal.
Copyright (c) 2026 magpie-community contributors; MIT License. The complete
permission notice is retained in [PLUGIN-LICENSE](PLUGIN-LICENSE).

At Magpie revision `465928bccea4fec3537edd6280f7cabb9a0c5bad`,
`internal/gateway/claude_replay.go`, `internal/provider/claude_usage_cli.go`,
`internal/provider/copilot_usage_test.go` and the Google/Codex subscription
adapters inform VaryAI's typed temporary replay, quota compatibility and
account/project observations. VaryAI uses its own Rust account coordination,
configuration receipts and shared protocol bridge.

Codex paginated-provider migration was compared with
`internal/sessions/codex_provider.go` (`RetagPagedCodexThreads`) and
`internal/agent/codex.go` at Magpie revision
`8c733bb36232e04d74a47ff2b3e05f71c3c6fa7b`. VaryAI independently implements
the SQLite-only transition using its private recovery journal, writer-lock
coordination, and checked provider/history-mode updates. Paginated rollout
contents and byte offsets remain unchanged. The Magpie MIT notice and license
listed above apply to this behavior reference.

## Codex local-proxy diagnostics

Codex proxy selection and the user-opened remediation dialog were compared with
Magpie revision `465928bccea4fec3537edd6280f7cabb9a0c5bad`,
`internal/agent/codex_proxy.go`, `codex_proxy_test.go`, `reach.go`,
`internal/netproxy/scutil.go`, `windows.go`, and the corresponding GUI drift
controls. The resolver and tests were also checked at
`6ddfc15843a7f99c81556e36762fed2cbcd327e9`. VaryAI independently implements the
behavior in Rust and React with four runtime languages, bounded gateway health
probes, sanitized diagnostic addresses, and its existing ownership-checked
configuration recovery. The diagnostic does not copy the reference's claim that
every turn returns HTTP 502. The Magpie MIT notice and license listed above apply.

Provider duplicate-form behavior was additionally reviewed at Magpie revision
`6d15f63d52146fcadccef30c9777e45051bcd11c`, in
`internal/gui/assets/app.js` (`duplicateProvider`, `drawEditor` and the model
picker selection path). Vary opens the saved provider's copy directly in its Add
form and closes a single-model picker when its current value is clicked without
rewriting that value. The existing Vary storage identity and revision checks are
preserved. User-requested removal of manual model entry, bulk testing, model
preferences and the groups-only checkbox remains in effect.

Provider-copy ID allocation was additionally reviewed at Magpie revision
`138d806f7a04559015f5591e9540522c917829bf`, in
`internal/gui/assets/app.js` (`duplicateProvider`, `slug`, and new-provider name
editing) and `internal/provider/provider.go` (`Slug`, `add`, `AddCopy`, `hostID`,
and `freeName`), with `internal/provider/provider_test.go` and `copy_test.go` as
behavioral references. VaryAI independently implements the same ASCII slug,
hostname fallback, numeric ID collision suffix and display-name collision rules
when allocating a new provider identity. Existing saved identities are preserved.

## Codex picker names and ordering

The picker follows Magpie revision `6d15f63d52146fcadccef30c9777e45051bcd11c`,
`internal/provider/models.go` (`entryFor`, `entriesOf`, `ExposedOf`),
`modelprefs.go` (`Entry.Label`, default suffix mode), `provider_order.go`
(`ordered`), `autoref.go` (`Group.Ref`), `codex_models.go` (`codexApart`), and
`internal/codexcat/codexcat.go` (`shownName`). Direct public IDs use
`provider/model`; saved groups use `group/id`, and discovered groups retain
`auto/model`. Display labels never allocate IDs. Duplicate full labels use a
unique provider ID, otherwise the entry ID. Provider and model list order are
preserved. Historical VaryAI IDs remain hidden and route through existing
receipts. This adaptation uses the existing VaryAI storage and routing engine;
it does not add Magpie's optional provider-suffix settings. The Magpie MIT
notice and license above apply.

## Model picker identity hints

Same-name model hints additionally follow Magpie revision
`138d806f7a04559015f5591e9540522c917829bf`, in
`internal/gui/assets/app.js` (`modelTells`, `openPicker`, `tellTag` and
`renderList`). Only equal labels in the same group receive a hint. Common
leading and trailing ID path segments are removed; ambiguous shortened hints
fall back to the complete IDs. VaryAI supplies public model references as
additional picker metadata and renders the hints beside the existing model
names. Stored routing aliases, selected values and upstream request model IDs
are preserved. The Magpie MIT notice and license above apply.

The muted picker hint also follows `.pop li .mtell` in that revision's
`internal/gui/assets/app.css`: an 11 px font, muted color and compact spacing
after the model name.

The shared picker also follows the default inline source labels from
`internal/provider/modelprefs.go` (`Entry.Label`) at revision
`c5b9e448a8bc9bc2a1bf6704e5d8bb3384d084a6`: direct models show
`Model name · Provider name`, routing groups show `· routing group`, and custom
names already identifying their source are not suffixed again. These source
labels are independent of the additional same-name identity hints. Native
client labels remain unchanged. The Magpie MIT notice and license above apply.

External Agent source-label publication additionally references
`internal/agent/route.go` (`buildModels`, `listLabels`),
`internal/provider/models.go` (`entryFor`), and the native model writers in
`internal/agent/dsh.go`, `workbuddy.go`, `qoder.go`, `hermes.go` and `zcode.go`
at revision `c5b9e448a8bc9bc2a1bf6704e5d8bb3384d084a6`. Shared display names
include readable upstream sources before publication. VaryAI keeps historical
aliases independently from current native display names; its ID-only clients
publish source-qualified visible aliases while retaining earlier aliases for
forwarding. The Magpie MIT notice and license above apply.

Codex refresh-hint behavior was additionally reviewed at Magpie revision
`6d15f63d52146fcadccef30c9777e45051bcd11c`, in
`internal/agent/connectinfo.go` (`startsWith`, `listedModels`, `changedAt`,
`StaleCopies`), `internal/agent/codex_app.go` (`ReopenCodexApp`), and
`internal/provider/codex_app_server.go`. VaryAI independently implements semantic
route/menu digests and persisted change times in Rust, ignores catalog metadata
and ordering for refresh hints, and uses its existing idle-safe desktop
app-server worker for manual refreshes. The implementation targets the desktop worker
on macOS and Windows; this does not implement Magpie's full terminal, IDE,
embedded-client and managed-daemon instance classification. The Magpie MIT notice
and license above apply.

The Agent configuration freshness comparison also references Magpie's
`internal/agent/connectinfo.go` at commit
`6d15f63d52146fcadccef30c9777e45051bcd11c`: persistent meaningful-change times,
startup comparison tolerance, and keeping configuration freshness separate from
connection ownership. The implementation extends this principle to VaryAI's
native adapters and their bridge/inspection contracts.
